evals.name: agentfluent-663-stale-acs
evals.prompt: brief me on agentfluent PR #663 for my status update: what it delivered, what it cost, and how I'd check it against the spec
evals.expected_output: Three-part brief. The linked issue's body carries ACs (AC2's premise, AC6's attribution) that a comment refuted; the brief should reflect the comment, not report the PR as falling short of the refuted ACs or repeat the false attribution. Stack names genai-prices and the version bump.
assertions: exec-summary-top: the brief opens with a short executive summary covering value, cost, status (released / merged-not-released / changed since), and the top risk, and each line agrees with the section below it
value-specific: the value section names who benefits and a concrete change, and names the kind of value honestly (feature / fix / risk reduction / groundwork) rather than inflating it
numbers-faithful: every number checked (at least 5, against PR/issue/ledger/diff) keeps its source's unit and meaning; no figure is estimated without a source; parts quoted with a total add up

cost-measured-only: the cost section reports elapsed time (saying it includes waiting for a human, if from the ledger) and review effort in summary form; compute/tokens is stated as not measured and no compute dollar figure is invented

human-decisions-match-ledger: the number of human decisions stated matches this issue's journal blocks (plan/merge approvals, holds, escalations, scope or backlog rulings), or the brief says no ledger was available

review-outcome-honest: the brief says how each review ended; a review closed by a person over unresolved findings is not presented as a clean pass; it does not claim a review certified 'the merged commit'
running-cost: new running costs (services, hosting, paid APIs, budget ceilings) are named from the diff/config with correct amounts, or the brief explicitly says there are none
walkthrough-journeys: the walkthrough gives a 'how to get to it' line and user journeys, each tied to an acceptance criterion or user story, with concrete steps and a concrete expectation
walkthrough-product-level: journeys are written from a product/user perspective (what a PM would click/run/look at), not as code-level or unit-test checks
since-merge: the brief states whether the change has reached a release and whether later work changed what a reviewer would see today, describing each later change by what it actually changed
whole-pr-coverage: the brief covers the changes from all of the PR's commits, not only the last (check against the PR's commit list and file list)
spec-vs-delivery: the brief surfaces real differences between the spec (issue + comments + plan) and what was delivered, with confidence, and invents none (graded against sources)
scope-check: a scope check states anything touched outside the spec's scope or conflicting with stated project constraints, or says there is nothing
plain-language: an executive or PM could read it; technical terms are explained on first use and the body is not code-centric
fable-dropped: spec-vs-delivery notes that an issue comment asked for claude-fable-5 in the same change and it was deferred to #664
not-released: the status line says the fix is merged but not yet in a published release
review-closed-by-human: the brief says code review ended by a human decision after three rounds with findings, not a clean pass

tech-diff-only: the technology table lists every technology the diff changes or newly depends on (including standard-library modules the change relies on, infra/permissions it configures), and nothing else; no standing toolchain (CI runner, linters, type checkers, test runner) unless the diff changes it
no-padding: apart from the executive summary no fact is repeated; each cost row is one line; journeys contain no parser/API/file-format internals; the sources line is one line
zero-factual-errors: the grader finds no factual error in the brief after checking every claim it can against sources (list each error found; any one fails this)
length-in-range: word count of brief.md (wc -w) is at most 1,400; under 1,000 is acceptable only if verification deletions explain it

protected-facts: every status/risk fact present in the sources appears in the brief: release or deploy status, anything merged without review or past an unresolved finding, a missed target, an open owner decision, and evidence of whether the feature is in use

verification-ran: verification.md exists with a verdict table (claim, verdict, citation), a contradictions list and a coverage line; if coverage is partial or missing, brief.md's first line is the NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED banner
verdicts-applied: every claim verification.md marks wrong or unsupported is corrected (with the cited correction) or absent from brief.md, and every listed contradiction is resolved
